### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a460b521bf82cc06dadf2d44e12415f4f261cc4` — the merge of head `21ac7e6a13b8562f78e7a88f432e22eedf709702` into base `b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a460b521bf82cc06dadf2d44e12415f4f261cc4 && git checkout 8a460b521bf82cc06dadf2d44e12415f4f261cc4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0 21ac7e6a13b8562f78e7a88f432e22eedf709702 && git checkout -B drift-repro b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0 && git merge --no-ff 21ac7e6a13b8562f78e7a88f432e22eedf709702

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b8615afaba7a9e6511b601ebc9f15deededea5b0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `21ac7e6a13b8562f78e7a88f432e22eedf709702`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/empty-projection-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-projection-refusal.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/get-record-id-projection.integration.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Inputs: card #27008 (body, triage `6458590093`, claim `6462987453`, os-dev-report `6464754246`, claim amendment `6465140445`), PR #27161 body and file list, `git diff origin/main...pr27161`, and the 49 check-runs on this head: every required run `success`, the rest `skipped` by path filter; none failed. The `Test Core (8/8)` red the amendment named on `2e447bbd` is green on this head, which carries the amendment's test fix (`21ac7e6a`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ObjectQL.find` / `findOne` refuse `fields: []` with `status: 400`, `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, before any driver read — right.** `assertProjectionNamesAField` is called at both entries (`engine.ts` ≈13523 and ≈13853) after `foldEngineOptionAliases` and `rejectUnknownEngineOptions` and before `lowerWhereFilterArray` and `getDriver`; `fields` and `expand` are both members of `ENGINE_FIND_OPTION_KEYS` (≈685), so the key gate never pre-empts the door. The status and code are the ones `projectionFieldsValue` (`protocol.ts` ≈4655) throws at the HTTP doors, so `mapDataError` answers both callers alike; the suite's REST-parity case pins it on the same engine.
2. **The refusal's remedy words are read off the published declaration, not copied — right.** `projectionNamesNoField()` memoises `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.shape.fields.safeParse([]).error.issues[0].message`, which is `PROJECTION_NAMES_NO_FIELD` from `transportProjectionArray(...).min(1, ...)` (`data-engine.zod.ts` ≈106–140). No spec edit, no second constant: the claim's "⛔ no second copy" line holds. The prefix text (`names no field in ...: got []. The query was not run: an empty projection was read as no projection, which answers every column.`) mirrors the door's sentence by design, and is the engine's own, not a copy of the constant.
3. **Absent and `null` `fields` still read every column; a non-empty projection and the #7589 unknown-plain tolerance are unchanged — right.** The door tests `Array.isArray(query.fields) && query.fields.length === 0` only; the `filtered.length > 0 ? filtered : undefined` fallback (≈13597 / ≈13900) is untouched. The claim's "⛔ No change to what an absent `fields` means" holds; three controls pin it.
4. **An `expand` entry's `fields: []`, at any depth, is refused at the parent's entry — right, and the placement is the correct one.** `expandRelatedRecords` (≈12590 ff.) resolves the sub-read through `this.find` inside a `try` whose `catch` retains the bare FK id ("A refusal is caught below and the bare FK id is retained"), so a refusal raised only in the sub-read would reach the caller as a silently unexpanded field. `assertExpandProjections` walks `expand[rel].fields` and recurses into `expand[rel].expand`, naming the path; non-object entries are skipped (the engine's `expand` is `z.record(z.string(), QuerySchema)`, ≈198, so no other shape reaches it). The two suites' expand cases pin one and two levels.
5. **A system-context read is refused too — right.** The door runs before any `context.isSystem` branch; the rule is about the shape. Pinned.
6. **The family is closed — right.** `count` and `aggregate` take no `fields` (not in their option-key sets; the key gate refuses it); `vectorFind` has no engine implementation; the scoped repository's reads delegate to these two entries. The REST doors already refused `select: []` before the engine, so the two gates agree rather than compete.
7. **`get_record` hands an authored `fields: []` to the engine unchanged and now fails with the refusal carried — right, and the claim amendment's ⛔ holds.** `projectionNamingId` (`crud-nodes.ts` ≈316) is byte-identical on `main` and this head: `[]` passes through (`fields.length === 0` returns `fields`); only the docblock changed. The node's `catch` (≈556–566) answers `success: false` with `refusalCarriedBy(err)`, so `innerRefusal.code` is `VALIDATION_ERROR`; the rewritten integration case pins exactly that, through the real `SqlDriver` stack. No `[]` → `undefined` normalisation, no consumer-side tolerance (Prime Directive #12).
8. **The amended integration test keeps one case per shape, none deleted — right.** The `for` loop over `['no fields', 'empty fields']` became two `it`s: the `no fields` control unchanged in substance, the `empty fields` case re-pinned from "whole-row read" to "refusal carried". Count 2 → 2; no assertion lost without a replacement at the same layer.
9. **Caller census re-taken at this head — right.** `git grep 'fields: \[\]'` over `packages ui examples apps skills` excluding tests: every hit is a result/declaration shape (analytics result rows, security field-reader answers, screen-node definitions, an orphan-sweep finding row), none an engine read option. The narrowing breaks nothing shipped in-repo.
10. **The new suite's driver double is faithful to the measured drivers — right.** It projects exactly and serves `[]` as every column (as `SqlDriver` and `InMemoryDriver` do), applies `limit`, throws on an unimplemented `$` combinator, and counts reads, so "zero driver reads" is measured. The two intermediate commits fixing the double answered the `check:objectql-double-limit` / `check:where-matcher` gates, both green here.

Doubtful, not wrong: the error message's `param` for the top level is spelled `'fields'` with literal quotes while the expand path is `expand['rel'].fields` without them. Cosmetic; both tests match their own form; no reader parses `param`.

Nothing in ① is wrong.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27008-engine-empty-projection-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). This matches the diff: an accept-set narrowing at a runtime entry, no key of any schema added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, no export or type change. Per AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3, a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner and disposition — right. The remedy sentence ("Leave `fields` out ... or name the columns") is the migration a narrowing owes. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset body, both line-initial — right. Nothing in the diff widens.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — right at this head and as the amendment ruled: no save or publish door refuses anything new; `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` and the nested `QuerySchema.fields` still accept `[]` (the run-time consequence for a flow author is the `success: false` carried refusal, judged in ① 7). The declaration gap is carried on #27166 (open, `pm:queue`, `domain:server`), not here.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: no changeset. The diff there is a docblock and a test; `projectionNamingId` is unchanged, so the package publishes no behaviour of its own. The behaviour a flow sees arrives through the `@objectstack/objectql` dependency, and that changeset's "Who sees it" names flows. Acceptable; `Check Changeset` agrees.
- `Skills-docs:` line, owed by triage for the narrowing arm: present (`content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`, a prose surface outside the at-tier scope; its sentence agrees with ① 1 and ① 4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` (needs_decision): an all-unknown non-empty projection (`fields: ['nope']`) still falls back to every column in-process via the #7589 tolerance, while the REST door answers `400 INVALID_FIELD`.** Not an empty projection from the caller, so outside card #27008's ruling, and the fallback is a KEPT ruling (engine.ts ≈13578, "ruled 2026-08-12"). Not a blocker for this PR. Escalated to the seat: it needs its own card and a ruling that either amends the #7589 edge (dev's option A, a narrowing with the ingress door's refusal) or pins and documents the fallback (option B). The dev's recommendation of A is reasoned, but a ruled tolerance is not reversed inside a review.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]` (class c): `GetRecordConfigSchema.fields` and nested `QuerySchema.fields` accept `[]` that the engine now refuses.** Answered: carried on #27166, open and queued; the claim amendment kept it there.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[1]` (observation): no in-repo flow or expand caller authors `fields: []`.** Answered: confirmed by this review's own re-census (① 9).
- **Claim amendment `6465140445`:** the `empty fields` case stays one case and is not deleted — verified (① 8); `crud-nodes.ts` is comment text only — verified (① 7); no other test file pins an empty projection read through `find` / `findOne` — none in the diff and none named in the report; no `service-automation` changeset owed — ② agrees.
- **Docs Drift Check (`6464749869`):** `crud-nodes.ts` yielded no anchor. The change there is a docblock; no page's claim moved. Nothing owed.
- **Premise:** `premise_still_valid: true`, re-measured on `07d18e69`; the Ablation and the red leg on `main` are reported in the PR body and are consistent with the diff. CI on this head is the gate verdict; no local run was needed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-y7p9hd`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**
